titulo: Should you flip a steak only once?
fuentes: McGee, McInerney, Harrus, 'The Virtual Cook: Modeling Heat Transfer in the Kitchen', Physics Today 52(11), 1999: https://physicstoday.aip.org/features/the-virtual-cook-modeling-heat-transfer-in-the-kitchen (computer model; flipping often cooks more evenly, probably faster)

America's Test Kitchen / Cook's Illustrated, 'The Effect of Flipping on a Crisp Burger and Steak Crust': https://www.americastestkitchen.com/cooksillustrated/how_tos/6362-the-effect-of-flipping-on-a-crisp-burger-and-steak-crust (flipping every minute: crispier crust, more evenly cooked meat; not for burgers)
ThermoWorks, 'Temping a Steak Doesn't Make It Dry': https://blog.thermoworks.com/temping-a-steak-doesnt-make-it-dry-debunking-a-kitchen-myth/ (overcooking, not probing, dries steak)

frases.texto: You've been flipping your steak only once.
frases.estilo: Dry and confident, like picking a fight with the grill master.
Short and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: The idea is simple: flip it often, and each side heats up a little, then rests a little.
The heat goes in more evenly, so the steak can cook more evenly, and often faster.
Food writer Harold McGee and colleagues modeled it, and America's Test Kitchen tested it: flipping every minute gave a crispier crust and more evenly cooked meat.
And the juices? Poking a steak doesn't drain it. Overcooking is what dries it out.
Heads up: this is for steaks over high heat, not burgers.
Want a golden crust tonight? Try flipping about every minute.
Send this to the friend who won't let anyone near the grill.
frases.estilo: Playful, with humor, as a punchline.
